question: Does faster recorded takeover initiation monotonically order recorded takeover success within the same driver and critical-event type?
decision: Use reaction time only as an initiation measure; determine whether these records falsify its substitution for recorded outcome before any model integration.

primary.pairs: All unordered pairs of valid trials with same driver ID and criticalEventType, one Success and one Failure.
primary.falsifier: At least one discordant pair falsifies deterministic monotone outcome substitution on these records. No discordant pair means not falsified here, never safety proof.
report: all driver-event strata including zero eligible

secondary: Outcome and reaction-time summaries for all task and event strata; all 30 task-event cells including empty ones.
Scenario end minus event onset minus reactionTime as recorded post-initiation follow-up; report nonpositive duration and never infer sustained recovery.
Reconcile all ten task counts, success ratios and reaction means against descriptor Table4 as a source-integrity check, not a new endpoint.
missingness: Keep every expected trial in coverage. Missing/invalid required fields give explicit issues, never zero or success. Primary classification incomplete if any required trial fails; valid-subset descriptive counts remain labeled.
validation: Duplicate identifiers, unexpected fields/values, nonfinite/noninteger time, negative time, inconsistent temporal order and extra data rows refuse that record. No silent coercion. Preserve exact source bytes.
comparator: Ordinary complete census and separately authored SQL self-join/count/aggregation supplied the same records. No speed or novelty claim.
exposure: Paper methods and Table4 aggregate outcomes seen before freeze. Archive member names and first30-byte local header inspected. No trial outcome payload acquired. Supplement notebook captured but code/output not read. This is exploratory retrospective analysis, not blind or preregistered.
